title: effective-catalog-v1 generation stamp (CAT-1)
description: Normative shape for catalog/gen-<digest>/stamp.json. See docs/content-paks.md in this repository. The canonical-bytes rule, the tree hash, the digest-names-the-directory rule, contributor/file ordering, the two validation levels, and the fail-closed table are business logic exercised by the fixtures in generations/, not by this schema alone.

schema.description: Exactly 1. A reader that sees anything else falls back to release defaults with stamp-schema-unsupported.

platform.description: Must equal the running platform and the `platform` of the merged systems.json/cores.json.

contributors.description: Ascending by `provider` in UTF-8 byte order. Ordering is normative because the digest is taken over canonical stamp bytes.

info_sha256.description: tree_sha256 over the .info directory. The release info dir is a compile input because its files are materialized into the generation; release_id alone would miss a partial manual copy.

provider.description: The install path (`mlp1/ScummVM.pak`) -- the identity pakrat_installs.install_path and apps.pak_dir key on. Never a resolved absolute root: MLP1 swaps /mnt/sdcard and /media/sdcard1 across reboots.

source_id.description: Card provenance only. jw_storage_source.id is "primary" or an index, so it names the card, not the pak, and can never identify a contributor.

files.description: EVERY declared file, ascending by `rel` in UTF-8 byte order. This is what makes swapping or deleting a .so without editing `provides` invalidate the stamp.
